title: Why the Nazca lines were drawn
summary: Scholars differ on the purpose of the Nazca lines, though most see religious meaning. Working out how they were made has been easier than knowing why.
why: Giant lines and figures cover a desert, and no one knows for sure why they were made.

notes.problem: Aveni rejected astronomical explanations generally, not only constellation links; third theory merged unrelated ideas.

question: Why did the Nazca people draw giant lines and figures across the desert?
evidence: Made roughly 500 BCE to 500 CE across Paracas and Nazca phases; some lines appear to follow aquifers; Hawkins and Aveni (1990) found astronomical explanations unsupported.
wouldSettle: Excavated offerings and dated activity along the lines showing how people used them.

theories.name: Astronomical markers
theories.idea: Kosok and Reiche proposed solstice sighting lines; later archaeoastronomers found the evidence insufficient.

theories.name: Water and fertility ritual
theories.idea: Reinhard linked the lines to worship of water and mountain deities; some follow underground water.

theories.name: Pilgrimage and gathering
theories.idea: Lines and figures served ritual gatherings that bound pilgrim groups sharing ancestors and beliefs.
